title: Semibrace existence on meet-semilattices: an attributed classification

native.creator: Alec Kriebel

proof: Under the workshop axioms every nonempty meet-semilattice, with any distinguished e, admits a semibrace via projection x·y=y. The empty carrier has no distinguished point.

In a simultaneous semibrace and L-algebra the diagonal, two identities, and separation force a=x∧e=x for every x, by applying S3 to a·x and a·a. Replacing e by y when x·y=e gives the reverse order implication, and if x∧y=x S3 with z=y gives x·y=e.

For a greatest e the historical operation f_x(y)=e when x≤y and x∧y otherwise satisfies identity, diagonal and separation, and commutativity of meet turns the S3 composition identity into the cycloid identity. Independently, f_x is right adjoint to g_x(t)=t for t≤x and x otherwise, which gives meet preservation. S3 follows by factoring through a=x∧y and, when x is not below z, using a≤x∧z iff a≤z. No finiteness, lattice, bottom or completeness requirement.

The older enumeration text with a monoid unit requires e to be top for both questions. The distinct Problem 10 operation with y in the else branch can fail meet preservation on the Boolean square even when it has other L-algebra properties. This classifies existence, not every compatible operation.

Independently verified adjunction and the Boolean square negative control.
